subject: Sprint Zero: cluster blueprint and blockstore operations — Acme Medical
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acmemed.com>, Acme Medical ITOps <itops@acmemed.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sprint Zero: cluster blueprint and blockstore operations — Acme Medical

Hi Lena / ITOps team,

Thanks again for the time earlier. Attached is a lightweight "Sprint Zero" checklist and a first-draft topology to help frame the kickoff for the on-prem private deployment. Goal for this thread: align on minimal access, network egress rules, storage topology (ephemeral NVMe for inference cache vs persistent block store for model weights), and a target maintenance window so we can schedule the initial install.

Key asks:
- Confirm whether the cluster will be fully air-gapped or allow a controlled outbound channel for telemetry and image pulls. If air-gapped, please confirm an internal registry/HTTP mirror or whether you want Redwood to provide an offline bundle.
- Target node counts and roles (examples below). If you don’t have exact numbers, a rough CPU/GPU ratio works.
- RPO/RTO requirements for model artifacts and whether you have an existing blockstore (iSCSI, Ceph, Pure) we should integrate with.
- Network constraints: any IP allowlists, egress proxies, or strict firewall zones we must plan for.

Initial recommendations (high level):
- Control plane: customer-managed control plane inside VPC; Redwood can run a companion control plane in your VPC or provide an offline operator bundle for air-gapped installs.
- Node pools:
  * control/management: 3x m4-type (or equivalent) nodes, 4–8 vCPU, 16–32GB RAM
  * inference (CPU): autoscaling pool, 8–32 cores/node, local NVMe cache (≥1TB) for model shards
  * inference (GPU): 1–3 GPU nodes (A100/A40 class) depending on throughput — recommend dedicated GPU node pool with 256GB+ RAM per node
- Storage: two-tier approach: fast local NVMe for KV/prefix/cache, persistent blockstore for model weights & artifacts (replicated, encrypted at rest). Consider Rook/Ceph if you need multi-node replication; otherwise a customer-managed SAN with iSCSI is acceptable.
- Ports: kube API (6443) limited to admin bastion; nodes need outbound 443 for image pulls unless offline. We’ll provide an explicit port list once you confirm air-gap status.

Attachments: sprint-zero-checklist.pdf (preflight items), topology-drawing-v1.png (draft), storage-iops-profile.csv (sample IOPS profiles).

Proposed next steps: please confirm the three items above by EOD Tue (2026-09-21) and we’ll lock an architecture review slot. If you prefer, we can run a 60-minute design session with your infra/ops on Wed 22 or Thu 23.

Best,
Monica Patel
Customer Solutions Manager — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Sprint Zero: cluster blueprint and blockstore operations — Acme Medical

Hi Monica — thanks for the summary and attachments. A few clarifications from our side before the design review:

1) Air-gap: procurement has signaled preference for a restricted outbound channel rather than a fully air-gapped install. We can allow outbound HTTPS via our proxy for specific FQDNs; complete offline bundles are acceptable if needed.
2) Privileged access: will you need kube-admin level credentials during install, or can you operate via a temporary service account with just the required chart CRDs? We prefer least-privilege.
3) Registry: we have an internal Harbor registry and can mirror images — would Redwood provide image list and tags to mirror?
4) Firewall / Ports: our security team asks for a specific port list (we cannot open wide ranges). Please provide exact ports for image pull, metrics, health checks, and control plane communication.
5) Compliance: SOC 2 evidence and an install-runbook are required by our procurement before we sign SOW. Can you attach the SOC 2 summary and the on-prem runbook?

Also: approximate numbers — we expect to start with 2 GPU nodes and ~6 CPU inference nodes, and will iterate; model weights are ~3TB total, daily delta of ~10–20GB.

Thanks — I can do Wed 22 at 10am PT for a design call.

—Lena
Director, Clinical Platforms | Acme Medical
lena.ortiz@acmemed.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acmemed.com>, Acme Medical ITOps <itops@acmemed.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Sep 2026 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sprint Zero: cluster blueprint and blockstore operations — Acme Medical

Thanks Lena — great notes. Quick answers inline below and an updated short port list attached.

1) Air-gap / registry: we can support both flows. If you mirror, we’ll provide a manifest of required images/tags and a Harbor sync script. If you prefer an offline install, we’ll provide a tarball and a signed manifest.

2) Privilege model: we prefer a temporary kube-admin service account for the initial install (rotation recommended). If your policy forbids admin-level access, we can provide an operator that installs with a reduced RBAC surface, but it typically requires a two-person install (your ops + Redwood onsite/remote).

3) Port list (short):
  - 443 TCP outbound (image pulls / control-plane telem if allowed)
  - 6443 TCP inbound (kube API) — restricted to installer/admin bastion IPs
  - 10250 TCP inbound (kubelet) — installer to nodes for orchestration; again limited to bastion range
  - 9100, 9090 (node-metrics / prometheus) — optional and can be proxied over HTTPS
  - 2379-2380 (etcd) — intra-control-plane; host-local only, no external exposure

4) SOC 2 + runbook: attaching a redacted SOC 2 summary and the on-prem runbook excerpt in the sprint-zero-checklist.pdf. If you need the full SOC 2 package we can start an evidence transfer via a secure portal (we’ll need an NDA/POC contact).

5) Storage sizing: for the ~3TB model store + daily 20GB delta I recommend:
  - Persistent blockstore: 10TB provisioned with 3x replication or appropriate RAID to allow headroom and GC/versions
  - Local NVMe cache: 1–2TB per GPU node for shard caching and KV cache; set eviction policy LRU with time-based TTLs
  - Backup: s3-compatible gateway or scheduled snapshots to your existing backup target; aim for 24–48h retention for active models and cold archive beyond that.

Operational notes:
- We'll recommend a canary rollout for model updates using weight-based traffic splitting to avoid large regressions.
- We'll provide an initial quantization/packing guide for GPU nodes to reduce memory footprint if you hit OOMs.

Next: Wed 2026-09-22 10:00 PT works for a 60-min call — I’ll send a calendar invite. Please confirm the bastion IP range and whether you want the offline bundle or mirrored registry for the install.

On Wed we’ll walk through the topology-drawing-v1.png and mark any rack-level constraints.

Best,
Monica
